questions.a: He extols Yahweh because Yahweh has drawn him up and has not allowed David’s enemies to rejoice over him.

questions.q: What did Yahweh do when David cried for help?
In what way did Yahweh restore David?
questions.a: Yahweh caused David to get well and restored him when he was about to die.

questions.q: What are the faithful told to do in remembrance of Yahweh’s holiness?
questions.a: The faithful are told to sing praise to Yahweh and to give him thanks.

questions.q: How long does Yahweh’s anger and favor last?
questions.a: Yahweh’s anger is only for a moment, but his favor is for a lifetime.

questions.q: What happens after weeping comes for a night?
What did David say when his life was going well?
questions.a: David said that he would never be shaken.

questions.q: What happened to David when Yahweh hid his face?
questions.a: When Yahweh hid his face, David was dismayed.

questions.q: What did David seek from the Lord?
questions.a: David sought favor from the Lord.

questions.q: What things is David asking Yahweh to do for him?
questions.a: David is asking Yahweh to hear him, to be gracious to him, and to be his helper.

questions.q: What has Yahweh done for David?
questions.a: Yahweh has turned David’s mourning into dancing, causing him to change from being sad to being joyful.

questions.q: What does David say his glory will do?
questions.a: David’s glory will sing praise to Yahweh and not be silent. He will give thanks to Yahweh his God forever.

commentary.text: Verses 1–5 The great things the Lord has done for us, both by his providence and by his grace, bind us in gratitude to do all we can to advance his kingdom among men, though the most we can do is but little. God's saints in heaven sing to him; why should not those on earth do the same? Not one of all God's perfections carries in it more terror to the wicked, or more comfort to the godly, than his holiness. It is a good sign that we are in some measure partakers of his holiness, if we can heartily rejoice at the remembrance of it. Our happiness is bound up in the Divine favour; if we have that, we have enough, whatever else we want; but as long as God's anger continues, so long the saints' weeping continues.

When things are well with us, we are very apt to think that they will always be so. When we see our mistake, it becomes us to think with shame upon our carnal security as our folly. If God hide his face, a good man is troubled, though no other calamity befal him. But if God, in wisdom and justice, turn from us, it will be the greatest folly if we turn from him. No; let us learn to pray in the dark. The sanctified spirit, which returns to God, shall praise him, shall be still praising him; but the services of God's house cannot be performed by the dust; it cannot praise him; there is none of that device or working in the grave, for it is the land of silence. We ask aright for life, when we do so that we may live to praise him. In due time God delivered the psalmist out of his troubles. Our tongue is our glory, and never more so than when employed in praising God. He would persevere to the end in praise, hoping that he should shortly be where this would be the everlasting work. But let all beware of carnal security. Neither outward prosperity, nor inward peace, here, are sure and lasting. The Lord, in his favour, has fixed the believer's safety firm as the deep-rooted mountains, but he must expect to meet with temptations and afflictions. When we grow careless, we fall into sin, the Lord hides his face, our comforts droop, and troubles assail us.
